subproblems.title: Smooth step profile on ℝ: 1 on (−∞, 1/2], 0 on [1, ∞), values in [0, 1], 3-Lipschitz
subproblems.statement: There is a C^infinity function φ : R → R such that (i) 0 <= φ(t) <= 1 for every t; (ii) φ(t) = 1 for every t <= 1/2; (iii) φ(t) = 0 for every t >= 1; (iv) φ is 3-Lipschitz, i.e. |φ(s) − φ(t)| <= 3|s − t| for all s, t ∈ R.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∃ φ : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ ∧ (∀ t, 0 ≤ φ t ∧ φ t ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ t, t ≤ 1 / 2 → φ t = 1) ∧ (∀ t, 1 ≤ t → φ t = 0) ∧ LipschitzWith 3 φ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–4 of the parent's supplied proof, which build the profile φ of the cutoff ζ(x) = φ(‖x − ξ‖/ρ). The Lipschitz estimate is from its step 3. In Lean, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) means C^infinity, and LipschitzWith 3 φ (3 : ℝ≥0) means |φ(s) − φ(t)| <= 3|s − t|.

Let S := Real.smoothTransition. Mathlib (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/SmoothTransition.lean) gives:
- S is C^infinity (Real.smoothTransition.contDiff);
- 0 <= S <= 1 (Real.smoothTransition.nonneg, Real.smoothTransition.le_one);
- S(s) = 0 for s <= 0 (Real.smoothTransition.zero_of_nonpos);
- S(s) = 1 for s >= 1 (Real.smoothTransition.one_of_one_le).

1. The bump g. Define g(t) := S(12(t − 1/2)) · S(12(1 − t)) for t ∈ R.
  (a) g is C^infinity. The maps t ↦ 12(t − 1/2) and t ↦ 12(1 − t) are affine, hence C^infinity. Composing them with S and multiplying keeps C^infinity. In particular g is continuous, so it is interval-integrable on every interval.
  (b) 0 <= g(t) <= 1 for every t, as a product of two numbers in [0, 1].
  (c) If t <= 1/2, then 12(t − 1/2) <= 0, so the first factor is 0 and g(t) = 0. If t >= 1, then 12(1 − t) <= 0, so the second factor is 0 and g(t) = 0.
  (d) If 7/12 <= t <= 11/12, then 12(t − 1/2) >= 12·(1/12) = 1 and 12(1 − t) >= 12·(1/12) = 1. Both factors equal 1, so g(t) = 1.

2. The normalizing constant. Let c := ∫_{1/2}^{1} g(s) ds.
  - By 1(d), ∫_{7/12}^{11/12} g = ∫_{7/12}^{11/12} 1 ds = 11/12 − 7/12 = 1/3 (intervalIntegral.integral_congr with the constant 1 on [7/12, 11/12]).
  - We have 1/2 <= 7/12 <= 11/12 <= 1, g >= 0 by 1(b), and g is integrable on [1/2, 1]. So the integral over the subinterval is at most the integral over the whole interval (intervalIntegral.integral_mono_interval): 1/3 <= c.
  - Hence c > 0 and c^{-1} <= 3.

3. The profile and its derivative. Define φ(t) := 1 − c^{-1} ∫_{1/2}^{t} g(s) ds (oriented interval integral).
  (a) g is continuous, so by the fundamental theorem of calculus (Continuous.integral_hasStrictDerivAt, or intervalIntegral.integral_hasDerivAt_right) u ↦ ∫_{1/2}^{u} g has derivative g(t) at every t. So φ is differentiable at every t with φ'(t) = −c^{-1} g(t). That is, φ is differentiable on R and deriv φ = −c^{-1}·g.
  (b) φ is C^infinity. By contDiff_infty_iff_deriv, ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ holds iff φ is differentiable and deriv φ is C^infinity. The first holds by (a). The second holds by (a) and 1(a), since a constant multiple of g is C^infinity.
  (c) φ is 3-Lipschitz. For every t, |φ'(t)| = c^{-1} g(t) <= c^{-1} · 1 <= 3, by 1(b) and step 2. A differentiable function R → R whose derivative has absolute value at most 3 everywhere is 3-Lipschitz, by the mean value inequality (lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_deriv_le).

4. Values of φ.
  (a) Case t <= 1/2. Every s between t and 1/2 has s <= 1/2, so g(s) = 0 by 1(c). Hence ∫_{1/2}^{t} g = 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_congr with the zero function) and φ(t) = 1 − c^{-1}·0 = 1.
  (b) Case t >= 1. By additivity over adjacent intervals (intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals; g is integrable on both pieces), ∫_{1/2}^{t} g = ∫_{1/2}^{1} g + ∫_{1}^{t} g. The second integral is 0, since g(s) = 0 for every s ∈ [1, t] by 1(c). So ∫_{1/2}^{t} g = c and φ(t) = 1 − c^{-1}c = 0 (as c ≠ 0).
  (c) Case 1/2 < t < 1.
    - g >= 0 and 1/2 <= t give ∫_{1/2}^{t} g >= 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_nonneg).
    - g >= 0 and [1/2, t] ⊆ [1/2, 1] give ∫_{1/2}^{t} g <= ∫_{1/2}^{1} g = c (intervalIntegral.integral_mono_interval).
    - Multiplying by c^{-1} > 0 gives 0 <= c^{-1} ∫_{1/2}^{t} g <= c^{-1}c = 1, so 0 <= φ(t) <= 1.
  Every real t falls in one of these three cases. In cases (a) and (b), φ(t) ∈ {1, 0} ⊆ [0, 1]. Hence 0 <= φ(t) <= 1 for all t.

5. Conclusion. φ satisfies every required property:
  - C^infinity, by 3(b);
  - values in [0, 1], by 4;
  - equal to 1 for t <= 1/2, by 4(a);
  - equal to 0 for t >= 1, by 4(b);
  - 3-Lipschitz, by 3(c). ∎

(Remark: in fact c = 5/12 by the symmetry S(s) + S(1 − s) = 1, but only c >= 1/3 is used.)
proof_key_steps: With S = Real.smoothTransition, g(t) = S(12(t − 1/2))·S(12(1 − t)) is C^∞, 0 <= g <= 1, g = 0 for t <= 1/2 and for t >= 1, and g = 1 on [7/12, 11/12]
c = ∫_{1/2}^{1} g >= ∫_{7/12}^{11/12} 1 = 1/3 (intervalIntegral.integral_mono_interval), so c > 0 and c^{-1} <= 3
φ(t) = 1 − c^{-1}∫_{1/2}^{t} g has deriv φ = −c^{-1} g by FTC (Continuous.integral_hasStrictDerivAt), so φ is C^∞ by contDiff_infty_iff_deriv
|φ'| = c^{-1} g <= c^{-1} <= 3, so φ is 3-Lipschitz (lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_deriv_le)
φ = 1 for t <= 1/2 (g vanishes on [t, 1/2]); φ = 0 for t >= 1 (adjacent intervals, g vanishes on [1, t]); 0 <= φ <= 1 for 1/2 < t < 1 since 0 <= ∫_{1/2}^{t} g <= c

subproblems.title: The radial lift x ↦ φ(‖x − ξ‖/ρ) of a C^∞ profile with φ = 1 on (−∞, 1/2] is C^∞
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ N, ξ ∈ R^m (Euclidean space EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), ρ > 0, and let φ : R → R be C^infinity with φ(t) = 1 for every t <= 1/2. Then the function ζ : R^m → R, ζ(x) := φ(‖x − ξ‖/ρ), is C^infinity.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (ξ : Rn m) (ρ : ℝ) (φ : ℝ → ℝ), 0 < ρ → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ → (∀ t, t ≤ 1 / 2 → φ t = 1) → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (fun x : Rn m => φ (‖x - ξ‖ / ρ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent's supplied proof, with the profile φ reduced to the two properties that step uses (φ is C^infinity, and φ = 1 on (−∞, 1/2]). In Lean, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) means C^infinity.

1. By contDiff_iff_contDiffAt, ζ is C^infinity iff it is C^infinity at every point. Fix x ∈ R^m. We show ζ is C^infinity at x in two cases: x = ξ and x ≠ ξ.

2. Case x = ξ.
  - Since ρ/2 > 0, the open ball B°(ξ, ρ/2) = {y : ‖y − ξ‖ < ρ/2} is a neighbourhood of ξ (Metric.ball_mem_nhds).
  - For y in this ball, dist(y, ξ) = ‖y − ξ‖ < ρ/2. Since ρ > 0, this gives ‖y − ξ‖/ρ < 1/2, in particular <= 1/2. The hypothesis on φ then gives ζ(y) = φ(‖y − ξ‖/ρ) = 1.
  - So ζ agrees with the constant function 1 on a neighbourhood of ξ.
  - Constant functions are C^infinity (contDiffAt_const), and being C^infinity at a point depends only on the germ (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). Hence ζ is C^infinity at ξ.

3. Case x ≠ ξ.
  - Then x − ξ ≠ 0, and y ↦ y − ξ is C^infinity (identity minus a constant).
  - The Euclidean norm of the inner product space R^m is C^infinity at every nonzero point (contDiffAt_norm), in particular at x − ξ. By the chain rule (ContDiffAt.comp), y ↦ ‖y − ξ‖ is C^infinity at x.
  - Dividing by the constant ρ keeps this (ContDiffAt.div_const), so y ↦ ‖y − ξ‖/ρ is C^infinity at x.
  - φ is C^infinity on R, so it is C^infinity at ‖x − ξ‖/ρ (ContDiff.contDiffAt). The chain rule again shows that ζ = φ ∘ (y ↦ ‖y − ξ‖/ρ) is C^infinity at x.

4. Every x falls in case 2 or case 3. So ζ is C^infinity at every point, hence C^infinity on R^m by step 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to C^∞ at every point (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt)
At x = ξ: ζ ≡ 1 on the open ball B°(ξ, ρ/2), a neighbourhood of ξ, so ζ is C^∞ at ξ (contDiffAt_const.congr_of_eventuallyEq)
At x ≠ ξ: y ↦ ‖y − ξ‖/ρ is C^∞ at x (contDiffAt_norm at x − ξ ≠ 0, chain rule, div_const), and composing with the C^∞ map φ gives C^∞ at x

subproblems.title: The radial lift of a K-Lipschitz profile has ‖Dζ(x)‖ ≤ K/ρ everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ N, ξ ∈ R^m (Euclidean space EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), ρ > 0, K ∈ ℝ≥0, and let φ : R → R be K-Lipschitz, i.e. |φ(s) − φ(t)| <= K|s − t| for all s, t. Put ζ(y) := φ(‖y − ξ‖/ρ). Then for every x ∈ R^m the Fréchet derivative of ζ at x satisfies ‖Dζ(x)‖ <= K/ρ (operator norm). In Lean this is fderiv ℝ ζ x, which is 0 wherever ζ is not differentiable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (ξ : Rn m) (ρ : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0) (φ : ℝ → ℝ), 0 < ρ → LipschitzWith K φ → ∀ x : Rn m, ‖fderiv ℝ (fun y : Rn m => φ (‖y - ξ‖ / ρ)) x‖ ≤ (K : ℝ) / ρ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent's supplied proof ("ζ is (3/ρ)-Lipschitz ... hence ‖fderiv ℝ ζ x‖ <= 3/ρ"), with the constant 3 replaced by a general K ∈ ℝ≥0.

1. Lipschitz estimate. Let y, z ∈ R^m.
  - The Lipschitz property of φ and ρ > 0 give
    |ζ(y) − ζ(z)| <= K·|‖y − ξ‖/ρ − ‖z − ξ‖/ρ| = (K/ρ)·|‖y − ξ‖ − ‖z − ξ‖|.
  - The reverse triangle inequality (abs_norm_sub_norm_le) gives |‖y − ξ‖ − ‖z − ξ‖| <= ‖(y − ξ) − (z − ξ)‖ = ‖y − z‖.
  - Hence |ζ(y) − ζ(z)| <= (K/ρ)·‖y − z‖ = (K/ρ)·dist(y, z).

2. So ζ is Lipschitz on all of R^m with the nonnegative constant K/ρ.
  - In Lean: LipschitzWith (K / ρ.toNNReal) ζ, via LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul and step 1.
  - The real value of the ℝ≥0 constant K / ρ.toNNReal is (K : ℝ)/ρ. This follows from NNReal.coe_div together with Real.coe_toNNReal (ρ.toNNReal coerces back to ρ because ρ >= 0).

3. If a function on a normed space is C-Lipschitz everywhere, its Fréchet derivative has operator norm at most C at every point (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz). At points where it is not differentiable, fderiv is 0 and the bound is trivial. Applying this with C = K / ρ.toNNReal at x, and rewriting C as (K : ℝ)/ρ by step 2, gives ‖fderiv ℝ ζ x‖ <= K/ρ. ∎
proof_key_steps: |ζ(y) − ζ(z)| <= (K/ρ)|‖y − ξ‖ − ‖z − ξ‖| <= (K/ρ)‖y − z‖ (Lipschitz φ, ρ > 0, abs_norm_sub_norm_le)
ζ is LipschitzWith (K / ρ.toNNReal), whose real value is K/ρ (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul, NNReal.coe_div, Real.coe_toNNReal)
norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz gives ‖fderiv ℝ ζ x‖ <= K/ρ at every x
